characters: Nuhu: an 11-year-old boy, slim, in a red-and-white PE kit and well-worn trainers.
Ewoenam: Nuhu’s friend, 11, in the same PE kit, with braids tied back, holding a stopwatch and a notebook.
Mr Amankwah: the PE teacher, broad-shouldered, in a navy tracksuit with a whistle.

narrationPlan.voice: Encouraging, down-to-earth voice with sporty energy
narrationPlan.pace: Energetic, with a calm finish (about 120 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Upbeat drums and brass, softening to a warm piano finish (placeholder)
culturalNotes: School sports days are an important event across Ghana. The story questions whether winning is the only success worth celebrating, without criticising competition.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Does the story keep respect for winners while adding another form of recognition?

teacherGuide.overview: A story about measuring your own progress. It supports a conversation about different forms of success without suggesting that medals do not matter.
learningGoals: Compare numbers with decimals and find differences.
Explain more than one kind of success.
Describe how to propose a change respectfully.
beforeReading: Ask: what is the difference between winning and doing your best?
whileReading: At page 5, ask learners to work out Nuhu’s improvement.
afterReading: Run a safe personal-best challenge in PE, such as a standing jump or timed skipping.
discussion: Why did Nuhu feel two feelings at once?
Why was Ewoenam’s notebook useful when she spoke to Mr Amankwah?
reflection: What skill would you like to improve, and how could you measure it?

mathsExtension.task: Nuhu’s first time was 21.4 seconds and his Sports Day time was 19.7 seconds. How much faster was he?
Find the mean of his four practice times: 21.4, 20.9, 20.3 and 19.8 seconds.
How much faster was his third Friday time than his first Friday time?

support: Use a number line to find differences between decimal times.
stretch: Write your own proposal to the school for a new kind of recognition, with evidence.

culturalNotes: School sports days are an important event across Ghana. The story questions whether winning is the only success worth celebrating, without criticising competition.
localiseThis: Keep all challenges safe for children’s ages and abilities; times are invented for the story.
Respect children with disabilities by offering personal-best measures that work for them.
